topics.topic: Canberra Drive EC Government Land Sale tender won by Santarli Realty, Heeton, Kay Lim and Sunray consortium
topics.known_state: A consortium of Santarli Realty, Heeton Holdings, Kay Lim Holdings and Sunray Group Holdings topped the tender for the 99-year leasehold executive condominium GLS site at Canberra Drive with a bid of $163.9 million (about $825 psf ppr), a new benchmark for EC land prices. The tender closed Oct 1 with 13 bids, the strongest EC land turnout since 2018; the top bid was 2.74% above the second-highest $159.43 million ($803 psf ppr) from a TID–Hong Leong Group JV, with other bids including $798 psf ppr (Apex Asia Development, BHCC Development, HDB Development consortium), $735 psf ppr (CDL) and a low of $361 psf ppr (Sim Lian Group). The 124,167 sq ft site can yield about 185 homes and is about a five-minute walk from Canberra MRT Station.

topics.topic: Mapletree Logistics Trust sale of Mapletree Northwest Logistics Park in Shanghai
topics.known_state: Mapletree Logistics Trust agreed to sell Mapletree Northwest Logistics Park in Shanghai for RMB323.0 million (around S$61.3 million), about 0.5% of its S$13.1 billion AUM.
Mapletree Logistics Trust reported 1QFY2026/2027 DPU of S$0,01816, up 0.2% YoY, with occupancy at 96.4% and aggregate leverage at 40.5%.

topics.topic: Keppel–StarHub talks over potential deal involving M1
topics.known_state: Keppel confirmed talks with StarHub over a potential deal involving its telco M1, which sits in Keppel's Non-Core Portfolio for Divestment.

Keppel's 1H2026 net profit fell 59% YoY to S$154.7 million, driven by a S$375 million loss from its Non-Core Portfolio for Divestment; profit excluding the non-core portfolio rose 25% to S$530 million.

topics.topic: Seatrium share buyback increase to S$200 million
topics.known_state: Seatrium doubled its share buyback to S$200 million, funded from existing cash.
Seatrium's 1H2026 profit attributable to owners rose 158.3% to S$372.9 million, helped by a one-off S$171.7 million disposal gain, while free cash flow remained negative at S$11.6 million.

topics.topic: DFI Retail Group takeover of Starbucks licensed operations in seven Asian markets via Maxim's stake transfer
topics.known_state: DFI Retail Group will take full control of Starbucks' licensed operations in Singapore, Thailand, Hong Kong, Macau, Vietnam, Cambodia and Laos under a reorganisation in which it transfers its 50% stake in Maxim's Caterers to Hongkong Caterers, which will become Maxim's sole shareholder. DFI will receive US$340 million in cash, intended for growth or special dividends, with completion expected by end-March 2027 and an immediate boost to revenue and profitability. The Starbucks business in the seven markets generated US$746 million (S$955 million) in revenue in 2025, and DFI plans to grow outlets from 1,110 to 1,350 between 2027 and 2029, initially focusing on Thailand and Vietnam. Hongkong Caterers will continue to operate Maxim's portfolio of over 1,000 restaurants and bakeries, including five brands in Singapore: Genki Sushi, sen-ryo, Yakiniku Like, Butahage and Uoharu.

topics.topic: IOI Properties acquisition of Shenton 101, vehicle holding Singapore's Shenton House
topics.known_state: IOI Properties Group Bhd agreed to acquire Shenton 101, the vehicle owned by group CEO Datuk Lee Yeow Seng holding Singapore's Shenton House, for $1.00, while settling $217.06 million of shareholder advances and consolidating Shenton 101's $376.23 million borrowings (both as of July 31, 2026), reversing the non-interested directors' August 2024 rejection of a similar proposal. Shenton 101 won the tender for the 25-storey Shenton House for $538 million in November 2023 and completed the purchase in June 2024. The deal, funded by internal funds and requiring Bank Negara Malaysia approval plus consents from Shenton 101's lenders and the Singapore Land Authority, is expected to complete in Q4 2026 and is projected to lift net gearing from 0.70 times (June 30, 2025) to 1.10 times. Redevelopment plans call for a 35-storey mixed-use landmark with Grade-A offices, a 165-key luxury hotel and retail space, expanding net lettable area from 20,276 sqm to 36,528 sqm, with Savills appraising the redevelopment site at $585 million and gross development value at $1.61 billion.

topics.topic: City Developments GET+ three-year strategy for FY2027 to FY2029
topics.known_state: City Developments Ltd (CDL) unveiled GET+, a refreshed three-year strategy targeting $5 billion of new investments and at least $6 billion of divestments over FY2027 to FY2029. Of the new investment budget, 60% is earmarked for Singapore, 30% for China and Japan, and 10% for other markets, spanning residential, commercial, hospitality and living sectors. Key moves include launching a 145-unit luxury development in Shanghai's Xintiandi in December, exiting Australia's non-hotel assets, and splitting the $8.6 billion directly held hotel portfolio into about $5 billion to retain, $1.8 billion to enhance and $1.8 billion to divest. CDL also aims to double assets under management from about $5 billion to $10 billion by FY2029.
